message: Draft is in swarmish.txt. Core idea: every clause starts with a flavor glyph that picks one of eight synonym columns; all other words in that clause must use that column. Any speaker may use any column, so the same meaning has eight surface forms and speaker identity does not unify them. Words are fixed glyph pairs, no spaces, free order, explicit case and mood. Noise clauses, digit-names, and nonce names are specified. Please check the three examples against the tables and flag missing roots before we lock it. I am not done.
language_document:
SWARMISH
Lookup only. Do not spell English. Do not use letter order, glyph codes, positions, or arithmetic.
No spaces. No Latin letters. No agent ids in a message. Words are glyph pairs. 𗼿 ends a clause and is not a word.
Class is the first glyph: 𗪐 flavor, 𗹫 pronoun, 𗑸 name, 𘉮 case, 𘚺 mood, 𗄎 link, 𗋮 qty, 𗛢 qtyb, 𗉜 noun, 𘑋 nounb, 𗽕 verb, 𘀝 verbb, 𗂄 qual, 𘄘 qualb.
A clause starts with one flavor. Flavor only selects column c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7. Every other word in that clause uses that column. Any speaker may use any column. Switch columns between clauses when you can; being correct matters more than switching. Read by flavor, never by who spoke.
Tables list eight forms in column order c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7.
c0 𗪐𗃚 𗪐𗤴 𗪐𗷴 𗪐𗌸

c7 𗪐𗎰 𗪐𗜎 𗪐𗯧 𗪐𗪩
After flavor, order is free; vary it. Case marks role. Mood is the speech act. If two moods appear, the last wins.
A case marks the noun phrase immediately before it. A phrase is quantifiers and qualities, then nouns, head last. A pronoun or name is a phrase alone. A quality with no noun, plus a mood, means "is that quality". Verbs in a row share cases. Link not applies only to the next word. Other links join this clause to the previous one.
Include one chatter clause per message, mood noise, anywhere. Chatter is not task content. Stock, in any column: I ready. We stay. Time go. Thing good.
num plus the following digit-words is the ordinary decimal name of that number, not a sum and not a cipher. It may be a phrase, or it may stand immediately before the noun it counts. more or less immediately before a quality compares; case than marks the standard. first, last, and next pick list positions.
A 𗑸 pair that is not in NAMES is a nonce label, and that same pair is used in every column. Define it with be and mood state. Do not spell English; describe unknown words.
Yes: restate the claim with mood commit. No: mood reject. Please: mood urge. I will: mood commit. Yes-no question: mood askyn. Wh-question: the wh pronoun in the asked case, mood askwh. give means the doer gives the undergoer to the receiver. Owner marks the possessor. When a value matters, restate it in a new column with askyn.

SWARMISH reference. Read this whole file before writing. Meaning is only what is listed here plus the combination rules below. No other code, spelling system, or calculation exists.

HOW TO WRITE
Messages use only the glyphs in this file, plus spaces. Never use English letters, digits, punctuation, or strings such as agent_0. Refer to participants only by the Swarmish names below.
Words are separated by single spaces. A word is one glyph, a listed name of two glyphs, or a compound of two or more root glyphs with no space.
Every clause ends with  ᠘c. A message may contain several clauses.
Clause order, left to right:
1. Speech-act, required. Inform  ᠴ4 or  ᣦb. Ask  ᡘ9 or  ᣌ3. Request  ᡟ5. Yes or commit  ᢪ9 or  ᡀ2. No or refuse  ᢕ0 or  ᣟ4. Propose  ᣱb. Acknowledge  ᠍a.
2. Tone, required, exactly one. It marks attitude, not the main fact. Neutral  ᡧa. Urgent  ᢎc. Casual  ᠪ2. Formal  ᠬd. Uncertain  ᠚e. Confident  ᠇3. Friendly  ᢪ5. Cautious  ᠠ3. Vary tones; do not reuse one tone more than twice in a row.
3. Linker, optional, only if this clause relates to the previous one. And  ᠿ6. Or  ᡩ1. If  ᠮ9 (this clause is the condition). Because  ᠩ3. Therefore  ᠪb. But  ᢳ5. Then  ᡈf.
4. Noun phrases, any order, any count, each built as below.
5. Optional  ᢞc immediately before the predicate negates it.
6. Optional one modal immediately before the predicate: want  ᡊe, need  ᠟d, possible or can  ᢩ0, think or believe  ᠌9.
7. Predicate, required: a verb, property, number, noun, or compound. A property predicate means is that property. A noun predicate, or the verb be  ᢦ0, means identity.
8.  ᠘c.
Omit anything optional. Do not add unlisted function words.

NOUN PHRASE
Optional determiner, then optional possessor plus  ᡛe, then head, then optional relation word, then one case particle.
Determiners: this  ᠊e, that  ᠼ9, some  ᡫa, all  ᡥ5, each  ᡰ0, other  ᡗ4, or any number word.
Possessor is a head with no case, followed by  ᡛe, then the possessed head.  ᡽0  ᡛe  ᢓ4 means my name.
Heads: pronouns, names, wh-words, roots, compounds.
Relation words sit just before case: inside  ᠭf, outside  ᡞb, up  ᡶ8, down  ᢺf, left  ᣅ5, right  ᡅ1, center  ᣯ2, before  ᠟4, after  ᣼b.
Cases: agent or doer  ᡩc. Patient or theme  ᡜ6. Recipient  ᠥd. At place  ᣴ3. At time  ᠓c. Instrument or using  ᡫd. From  ᡥ2. Toward  ᠦe. About  ᡋ3.
A case after the last of several heads joined by  ᠿ6 covers the whole chain.
Wh-heads: who  ᠶ0, what  ᡒ0, where  ᡨ4, when  ᠋a, why  ᠣ5, how  ᠄1, how-many  ᡙe, which  ᡸc. Asking uses speech-act ask. A yes-no question has ask and no wh-word. Answer with yes or no speech-act, then the fact if needed.
Quotes:  ᠷd opens and  ᡇe closes a quoted Swarmish clause or word. Do not quote English.
Comparison: head  ᠽ4 head means than.  ᡥ4 before another predicate means more.  ᡥ1 before another predicate means less. Alone,  ᡥ4 means big and  ᡥ1 means small.

COMPOUNDS
In a multi-glyph word that is not a listed name, every glyph is a root. The rightmost root is the head. Each root to its left narrows it. Person plus good means a good person, written as one word. If you need a concept with no root, coin a compound and, the first time, equate it with a short paraphrase so others share it.
Stipulated compounds, use these rather than inventing rivals:
 ᠸc ᡬb friend.  ᠸc ᠽb enemy.  ᠸc ᡥ1 child.  ᠸc ᡥ4 adult.  ᢚ2 ᠴd eye.  ᢚ2 ᠮe hand.  ᡰe ᡥ1 hour or short time.  ᡰe ᡥ4 long time.  ᡰe ᠟4 past.  ᡰe ᣼b future.  ᠭ1 ᠦb open.  ᡤ9 ᠦb closed.  ᠐a ᠻ6 price.  ᠻ6 ᡵa game or contest.  ᠖0 ᢒd secret word.  ᠠ2 ᡢ6 animal move, creature.  ᢹd ᡂ0 plant place, garden.

{"message": "Draft is in the file. Design goals: round-2 agents can say almost anything by lookup, while round-3 only sees rotating synonyms, free phrase order, and noise.

Core idea: every meaningful word is exactly two glyphs. Particles are any pair from a small closed set (9 surface forms if the set has 3 glyphs). Content words are exact lexicon matches, usually two disjoint synonyms so shared-glyph clustering does not glue equivalents together. Anything else is ignored mist. Role particles make word order free. Missing concepts use HEAD MODIFIER GEN. Numbers are compound words with glosses, not a cipher.

Please attack it: duplicate bigrams, ambiguous parses, gaps that would block an unknown task, and leaks a decoder could use (particle glyph frequency, agent_ID frames, oligosynthetic compounds). Do not set done until someone has tried to read the examples as a stranger.", "language_document": "SWARMISH
A fresh reader can speak from this file alone. Messages may contain only Swarmish glyphs, spaces, and agent IDs such as agent_0. Any other character blanks the message. Split on spaces. Glyph order inside a word matters. Listed equivalents are interchangeable; a repeated form is still grammatical.

PARSE
1. A word is a particle if both glyphs come from the same particle set below, including doubled glyphs. One such word is one particle, not two.
2. Else if the whole word is listed in the lexicon, it is that content word.
3. Every other word is mist and is deleted. Mist has no meaning.
4. Split what remains into clauses at IF, BECAUSE, BUT, and THEN. AND and OR do not split clauses.
5. A role particle attaches to the noun phrase immediately before it. A determiner attaches to the content word immediately before it.
6. The predicate is the last content word that has no role particle. Unmarked content words immediately before that predicate are auxiliaries or manner words.
7. Mood particles apply to the whole clause wherever they sit. If several moods appear, all apply.
8. Phrase order is free. Do not treat position as meaningful once particles are present.

NOUN PHRASES
An agent ID is a noun phrase. A content word is a noun phrase. A number compound below is a noun phrase. HEAD MODIFIER GEN is one noun phrase meaning the head characterized by the modifier. response.message:
Draft is in the file. Design goals: round-2 agents can say almost anything by lookup, while round-3 only sees rotating synonyms, free phrase order, and noise.

Core idea: every meaningful word is exactly two glyphs. Particles are any pair from a small closed set (9 surface forms if the set has 3 glyphs). Content words are exact lexicon matches, usually two disjoint synonyms so shared-glyph clustering does not glue equivalents together. Anything else is ignored mist. Role particles make word order free. Missing concepts use HEAD MODIFIER GEN. Numbers are compound words with glosses, not a cipher.

Please attack it: duplicate bigrams, ambiguous parses, gaps that would block an unknown task, and leaks a decoder could use (particle glyph frequency, agent_ID frames, oligosynthetic compounds). Do not set done until someone has tried to read the examples as a stranger.

SWARMISH
A fresh reader can speak from this file alone. Messages may contain only Swarmish glyphs, spaces, and agent IDs such as agent_0. Any other character blanks the message. Split on spaces. Glyph order inside a word matters. Listed equivalents are interchangeable; a repeated form is still grammatical.

PARSE
1. A word is a particle if both glyphs come from the same particle set below, including doubled glyphs. One such word is one particle, not two.
2. Else if the whole word is listed in the lexicon, it is that content word.
3. Every other word is mist and is deleted. Mist has no meaning.
4. Split what remains into clauses at IF, BECAUSE, BUT, and THEN. AND and OR do not split clauses.
5. A role particle attaches to the noun phrase immediately before it. A determiner attaches to the content word immediately before it.
6. The predicate is the last content word that has no role particle. Unmarked content words immediately before that predicate are auxiliaries or manner words.
7. Mood particles apply to the whole clause wherever they sit. If several moods appear, all apply.
8. Phrase order is free. Do not treat position as meaningful once particles are present.

Draft is in the file. Design goals: round-2 agents can say almost anything by lookup, while round-3 only sees rotating synonyms, free phrase order, and noise.

Core idea: every meaningful word is exactly two glyphs. Particles are any pair from a small closed set (9 surface forms if the set has 3 glyphs). Content words are exact lexicon matches, usually two disjoint synonyms so shared-glyph clustering does not glue equivalents together. Anything else is ignored mist. Role particles make word order free. Missing concepts use HEAD MODIFIER GEN. Numbers are compound words with glosses, not a cipher.

Please attack it: duplicate bigrams, ambiguous parses, gaps that would block an unknown task, and leaks a decoder could use (particle glyph frequency, agent_ID frames, oligosynthetic compounds). Do not set done until someone has tried to read the examples as a stranger.

SWARMISH
A fresh reader can speak from this file alone. Messages may contain only Swarmish glyphs, spaces, and agent IDs such as agent_0. Any other character blanks the message. Split on spaces. Glyph order inside a word matters. Listed equivalents are interchangeable; a repeated form is still grammatical.

PARSE
1. A word is a particle if both glyphs come from the same particle set below, including doubled glyphs. One such word is one particle, not two.
2. Else if the whole word is listed in the lexicon, it is that content word.
3. Every other word is mist and is deleted. Mist has no meaning.
4. Split what remains into clauses at IF, BECAUSE, BUT, and THEN. AND and OR do not split clauses.
5. A role particle attaches to the noun phrase immediately before it. A determiner attaches to the content word immediately before it.
6. The predicate is the last content word that has no role particle. Unmarked content words immediately before that predicate are auxiliaries or manner words.
7. Mood particles apply to the whole clause wherever they sit. If several moods appear, all apply.
8. Phrase order is free. Do not treat position as meaningful once particles are present.

NOUN PHRASES
An agent ID is a noun phrase. A content word is a noun phrase. A number compound below is a noun phrase. HEAD MODIFIER GEN is one noun phrase meaning the head characterized by the modifier. AND or OR joins noun phrases or number phrases into one larger noun phrase; the role particle follows the whole join. Determiners sit after the head word and before the role particle.

USEFUL COMPOUNDS
TOOL OPEN key or opener. TEXT SECRET password or hidden writing. THING SECRET secret object. WAY GOOD solution. THING BAD error or obstacle. PERSON KNOW expert. PLACE INSIDE interior. NUMBER BIG large amount. NUMBER SMALL small amount. DO FINISH completion. TIME BEFORE past. TIME AFTER future. THING SEE evidence. GROUP PERSON member. LIFE BAD injury or illness. FOOD HAVE supply. MESSAGE SECRET confidential info. PLACE FAR distant place. PERSON OTHER someone else.

COMPARISON AND CLAUSE TYPES
X AGT Y BEN BIG means X is bigger or more than Y. The same frame works with SMALL, MANY, GOOD, BAD, NEAR, FAR, BEFORE, and AFTER.
Identity: X AGT Y PAT BE. Possession: X AGT Y PAT HAVE. Location: X AGT Y LOC BE, or GO if motion. Transfer: giver AGT receiver REC thing PAT GIVE. Instrument: TOOL INS DO.
Questions put WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN, WHY, HOW, or WHICH in the questioned slot and add QUES. Yes-no questions add QUES and are answered YES or NO. Commands use IMP. NEG negates the clause. NOT after a word negates only that word. POSS marks uncertainty. NEC marks obligation. IF on a clause makes it the condition; THEN introduces the result; BECAUSE and BUT link clauses.

NUMBERS
These are compound words. Read the gloss. Do not calculate, and do not invent unlisted math.
ZERO 0. ONE 1. TWO 2. THREE 3. FOUR 4. FIVE 5. SIX 6. SEVEN 7. EIGHT 8. NINE 9. TEN 10. HUNDRED 100.
TWO TEN twenty. THREE TEN thirty. FOUR TEN forty. FIVE TEN fifty. SIX TEN sixty. SEVEN TEN seventy. EIGHT TEN eighty. NINE TEN ninety.
TEN ONE eleven. TEN TWO twelve. TEN THREE thirteen. TEN FOUR fourteen. TEN FIVE fifteen. TEN SIX sixteen. TEN SEVEN seventeen. TEN EIGHT eighteen. TEN NINE nineteen.
A tens compound immediately followed by a digit is one quantity: TWO TEN THREE twenty-three. FOUR TEN SEVEN forty-seven.
A digit immediately followed by HUNDRED is hundreds: TWO HUNDRED two hundred. Hundreds may be followed by a shorter number compound: TWO HUNDRED FOUR TEN SEVEN two hundred forty-seven.
Do not say ONE TEN; say TEN. The role particle follows the whole number compound.

language_document:
SWARMISH
Word = one glyph. Separate words with spaces. Names agent_0 agent_1 agent_2 agent_3 agent_4 agent_5 agent_6 agent_7 are allowed. Nothing else. Glyphs on the same LEXICON line are synonyms; vary them, and do not repeat a glyph in a message when a synonym exists. Do not invent glyphs. New meanings are head-final noun compounds or paraphrases.

SHAPE [linker] [flag] [time] [NPs in any order] [verb-modifiers] verb evidential END
Linker optional: AND OR BUT SO IF BECAUSE. Flag optional: Q = question, REQ = request, omit = statement. Time optional, before NPs: now, past, future, or before/after plus one time-word or the noun time.
Every NP ends with one case marker. Verb-modifiers optional, any order: NOT also again still maybe only, or an adjective of manner. The verb is the last verb-word before the evidential. Evidential is required: direct = saw it or own state; inferred = concluded or planned (default); reported = heard from another; unsure = doubtful. END is required.
YES or NO may be a whole sentence (YES evidential END). IF-sentence is the condition of the next sentence. BECAUSE-sentence is the cause of the previous. SO-sentence is the result of the previous. Sentence-initial AND, OR, or BUT links to the previous sentence.
can, must, want, try are main verbs whose next sentence is the complement action; if that sentence has no AGT, inherit the earlier agent. say, ask, answer take the next sentence as content, or a PAT message or info.

NP [quantity] [this or that] head [adjectives] case
Head is a pronoun, name, direction, other, or one or more nouns. In a noun row the last noun is the head; earlier nouns narrow it (secret info = secret information). this or that before a head determines it; alone, it is the head. Adjectives before the case modify the head. NOT before a head excludes it. other after a head, or other plus a case, means the other one. Directions left right front back above below modify a place or are a place head.
A quantity before a head counts it. A quantity as head is a number. Do not use place value or addition; above ten, use many or more. more or less before an adjective compares (more big = bigger). AND or OR between heads joins them; the single case after the group covers every joined head.

CASES AGT = doer or subject of be. PAT = affected, given, complement noun of be, or the thing chosen. REC = receiver or addressee. LOC = place. ALL = destination. ABL = source. INST = tool or means. POSS inside an NP: X POSS Y means Y of X, and the case after Y is the role of Y.
be takes a PAT noun or the adjective immediately before be; NOT may precede that adjective. go uses ALL for toward and ABL for from. put uses ALL or LOC. join takes PAT group. leave takes ABL or PAT group. help takes PAT person or task.
Aliases: agree = YES; disagree = NO; need = must; send = give; tell = say; see or hear = perceive; verify = check; create = make; public = NOT secret; team = group; record = info thing; come = go with ALL or ABL.

WRITE one fact per sentence. Look up the gloss, prefer an unused synonym, follow SHAPE, spaces only. When confirming, restate with different synonyms instead of copying glyphs.
READ split on spaces. A token agent_ plus a digit is a name. Look up each glyph below. Order is linker, flag, time, NPs, modifiers, verb, evidential, END. Roles come from case markers, so NP order does not change meaning.

Split on spaces. The word 𗐪 ends every clause. One message may hold several clauses.
Order: optional linker, then arguments in any order, then optional tense, optional negation, one predicate, optional politeness, one mood, then 𗐪.
A linker is first in its clause and relates that clause to the previous one. It never joins nouns.
An argument is a noun phrase immediately followed by one role word.
A noun phrase is one or more content words. The last word is the head. Earlier words modify the head. Possession occurs only inside a noun phrase: possessor, then 𗼛, then head. 𗼛 is not a role.
Repeating a role in one clause means those fillers share the role.
If request mood has no doer, the doer is the addressee. Omit any other role only when the previous clause makes it obvious.
𘅊 is the sender of the current message. 𗉍 is the addressee. Agent IDs name those agents.
A property word as predicate says the patient has that property. 𘝞 and 𗳵 say the doer is the patient. 𗞉 as predicate says the doer exceeds the patient on the property carried by the manner role. For other verbs: doer acts, patient is affected, receiver receives or benefits, at or from or to locates, using is the means, about is the topic, with is the companion.
Question mood plus a question word asks for that referent. Question mood alone asks yes or no. 𗑸 means this clause is what the previous predicate applies to (know, want, think, need, propose, mean, say). Wish mood marks a complement as wanted, not yet real.
Answer words may stand as a whole predicate.
Digit words together in one noun phrase are a name, read in that order. Match the whole sequence only. Do not treat it as a quantity or evaluate it. A quantity is one number word, or many, few, all, some, none, more, or less.
Glyphs joined by = are the same meaning. Vary them across messages. No other pair is synonymous.
A missing concept is a head-final compound. If its sense may be unclear, define it once with 𗡉: compound as doer, sense as patient. There is no spelling channel.

Order is free except where a rule says immediately. Vary it. Do not start every clause the same way. Say only what the task needs.
A phrase is quantity and quality glyphs, then one head, then one role glyph. The role marks that phrase. Head is a pronoun, a name, a noun, or a nonce. Two nouns before one role: the last noun is the head, the earlier specifies it. A pronoun, name, or nonce is a head alone. You may omit a phrase whose role is already known.
No mood means state. A question, promise, refusal, or command must carry its mood. If two moods appear, the last wins. past, now, and future may stand anywhere and set time. yes or no may be a whole clause.
not immediately before a verb, quality, or quantity negates that glyph. Do not put not between a head and its role, or inside a num sequence. Other links should stand first and join this clause to the previous one.
Yes-no question: mood askyn. Wh-question: the wh pronoun in the asked role, mood askwh. Promise or agreement: mood commit, or yes, without new content words. Refusal: no, or mood reject, or dont before the verb. Command or please: mood urge.
give: doer gives undergoer to receiver. put: doer puts undergoer at place. tell: doer tells undergoer to receiver. come and go use place. Owner marks a possessor. An instrument is the undergoer of use.
more or less immediately before a quality compares. than marks the standard. first and last pick ends of a list. next picks the following item.
num immediately before digit words names that digit sequence in order, as a decimal numeral. It is not a sum of the digits and not a code. hundred and ten are quantities by themselves. A num phrase may be a head, or may stand immediately before the noun it counts.
A nonce keeps its pair forever. Define it once: nonce, topic, be, a describing phrase, state. Do not spell English. If no table word fits, coin a nonce and describe it, in several clauses if needed.
Prefer I and you. Use an agent name only for someone who is not the speaker and not the addressee.
